predecessors.name: Lawik Dynasty
predecessors.text: Ghazna, taken from the local Lawik rulers in 962

predecessors.name: Samanid Empire
predecessors.text: the eastern Khurasanian towns of Balkh, Tirmidh and Herat

successors.name: Ghurid dynasty
successors.text: Lahore and the Punjab, annexed by Muhammad of Ghor in 1186

ledger.x: 962: Alp-Tegin takes Ghazna from the local Lawik rulers.
977: Sabuktigin, elected by the Turkic garrisons, founds the Ghaznavid dynasty proper.
978: Sabuktigin invades Rukkhaj and Bust in the south.
986: the Hindu Shahi king Jayapala marches on Ghazna.
988: Sabuktigin wins the second battle of Laghman.
988: Sabuktigin takes the lands from Lamghan to Peshawar.
998: Mahmud, newly Sultan of Ghazna, is confirmed in Balkh, Tirmidh and Herat.
999: the Samanid lands of Khorasan pass to Mahmud, the Oxus becoming the border.
1001: Mahmud takes Peshawar and Gandhara from the Hindu Shahis.
1001: the war with the Hindu Shahis moves east of Peshawar.
1002: Mahmud conquers Sistan.
1006: Mahmud marches on the Emirate of Multan.
1008: after Chach the Ghaznavids annex the Hindu Shahi land from the Indus to Nagarkot.
1008: the Hindu Shahi wars end at Chach (31 December 1008); the Punjab is annexed.
1010: Mahmud subdues Multan.
1010: the Multan war ends with the October expedition.
1011: Mahmud conquers Ghor.
1017: Mahmud conquers Khwarazm.
1021: the Punjab is officially annexed.
1026: Sindh begins to pay tribute.
1029: Mahmud enters Ray.
1030: the Kakuyids retake Ray.
1030: Hamadan and Isfahan fall to Mas'ud.
1030: Sindh's tribute ends with Mahmud's death.
1033: Ray is back under Ghaznavid governors.
1034: Khwarazm breaks away under Harun.
1034: Mas'ud cedes Nasa, Farava and Dihistan to the Seljuks.
1035: the Seljuks, driven from Khwarazm, enter Khorasan.
1037: the Kakuyid Muhammad occupies Ray again.
1040: the Seljuks win Khorasan at Dandanaqan.
1040: Dandanaqan costs the Ghaznavids Persia and Central Asia.
1041-1050 (bridge): Mahipala of Delhi takes Hansi and Thanesar from Mawdud.
1060: Ibrahim invades Ghur at the nobles' request.
1148: the Ghurids beat Bahram-Shah at Ghazni.
1152: the Ghurid attempt on Ghazna ends with Ala al-Din Husayn's defeat.
1161 (latest year the pages allow): Ala al-Din Husayn of Ghor takes Zamindawar, Bust and Bamiyan.
By 1161 (no page gives the year): Multan has passed from the Ghaznavids to the Qarmatians.
1162: the Oghuz Turks seize Ghazni; the Ghaznavids retreat to Lahore.
1162: the capital moves from Ghazna to Lahore.
1162: with Ghazni gone the Ghaznavids keep Lahore and the Punjab.
ledger.cp: Ghuzz Turks, Ghurids and local rulers (pages silent)

ledger.x: 1178: Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad of Ghor invades Ghaznavid Punjab.
1179: the Ghurids seize Peshawar.
1186: the Punjab war ends with the fall of Lahore.
1186: Muhammad of Ghor takes Lahore and ends the Ghaznavids.

wars.name: Ghaznavid-Hindu Shahi wars
wars.outcome: Ghaznavid victory: Sabuktigin took the lands from Lamghan to Peshawar (988), Mahmud won at Peshawar on 28 November 1001 and at Chach on 31 December 1008 and annexed the region from the Indus to Nagarkot.

wars.name: Ghaznavid intervention in the Samanid civil war
wars.outcome: Sabuktigin and Mahmud fought for the Samanid emir against the rebels Fa'iq and Abu Ali (Khorasan taken 23 October 994, Nishapur lost and retaken 995); in 998 Mansur II confirmed Mahmud in Balkh, Tirmidh and Herat and the Oxus became the border.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Sistan
wars.outcome: Mahmud dethroned Khalaf ibn Ahmad and ended the Saffarid dynasty.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Multan
wars.outcome: Mahmud marched on Multan in March-April 1006 and 'successfully subdued' it in October 1010.

wars.name: Ghaznavid invasion of Kashmir
wars.outcome: 'In 1015, Mahmud unsuccessfully attacked Kashmir'; after two failed attempts he did not try again.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Khwarazm
wars.outcome: Mahmud beat the rebels on 3 July 1017 and captured Gurganj; Khwarazm broke away again under Harun in 1034.

wars.name: Ghaznavid expedition to Kannauj and Mathura
wars.outcome: Mahmud took the seven forts of Kannauj (arrived 20 December 1018) and plundered Mathura; the cities were sacked, not annexed.

wars.name: Ghaznavid campaign in Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Mahmud invaded Transoxiana in September 1024; Qadir Khan allied with him at Samarkand on 29 April 1025 and Mahmud 'left Samarkand to Qadir Khan'.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of the Jibal
wars.outcome: Mahmud entered Ray on 26 May 1029; Mas'ud took Hamadan and Isfahan (January 1030); Ray was lost to the Kakuyids in 1030.

wars.name: Ghaznavid-Kakuyid struggle for Ray
wars.outcome: Kakuyids wrested Ray in 1030; Mas'ud named a governor of Jibal in 1033 (Ray back under Ghaznavid governors by then, ledger confidence 1) and invaded western Iran in 1035; Muhammad 'once again occupied Ray' in 1037/8.

wars.name: Battle of Dandanaqan
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory near Merv on 23 May 1040; Khorasan annexed by the Seljuks, the Ghaznavids restricted to Afghanistan, Pakistan and northern India.

wars.name: Ghaznavid-Seljuk clash at Sakalkand
wars.outcome: Ibrahim sent an army into Sakalkand in January 1073 after about fourteen years of peace; the Seljuks drove it out.

wars.name: Sanjar's campaign against Bahram-Shah
wars.outcome: After Bahram stopped paying tribute, Sanjar marched on Ghazna in 1135 and Bahram fled to Lahore; he remained a Seljuk tributary.

wars.name: Ghurid-Ghaznavid war for Ghazni
wars.outcome: Sayf al-Din Suri beat Bahram at Ghazni in 1148; Bahram retook it; Ala al-Din Husayn sacked it (1150/1151) and was beaten and captured by Sanjar at Nab in 1152.

wars.name: Oghuz seizure of Ghazni
wars.outcome: Oghuz Turks seized Ghazni in 1161/2 and Khusrau Malik retreated to Lahore; the Ghurids reconquered it from the Ghuzz in 1173.

wars.name: Ghurid conquest of the Ghaznavid Punjab
wars.outcome: Muhammad of Ghor invaded in 1178, took Peshawar in 1179/80, was bought off at Lahore in 1181/2 and captured Lahore in 1186, ending the dynasty.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened; the Oxus border of 999-1017 follows a river, the Seljuk frontier after 1040 is undefined, and the Punjab limits are approximate.
